::: {#thm-monte-carlo-se}
#### Monte Carlo standard error of a simulation estimate

Let $T_1, \ldots, T_M$ be the estimates of $M$ [replications](#def-replication) of a [simulation study](#def-simulation-study),
which are [IID](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-iid) with expectation $\E{T}$ and finite variance $\Var{T}$.
Then the [simulation estimate](#def-simulation-estimate) $\bar T_M$ is [unbiased](estimation.qmd#def-unbiased) for $\E{T}$,
and its [Monte Carlo standard error](#def-monte-carlo-standard-error) is

$$\SE{\bar T_M} = \frac{\SD{T}}{\sqrt{M}}.$$
:::

::: proof
By [the mean and variance of a sum of IID random variables](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/limit-theorems.html#thm-sum-iid-moments),
the sum $S_M \eqdef \sumto{m}{M} T_m$ has $\E{S_M} = M\,\E{T}$ and $\Var{S_M} = M\,\Var{T}$.
Since $\bar T_M = S_M / M$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{\bar T_M} &= \frac{\E{S_M}}{M} && \text{(constants factor out of expectations)}\\
&= \E{T} && \text{(substitute $\E{S_M}$ and cancel $M$)}\\
\Var{\bar T_M} &= \frac{\Var{S_M}}{M^2} && \text{(a constant factor $c$ scales variance by $c^2$)}\\
&= \frac{M\,\Var{T}}{M^2} && \text{(substitute $\Var{S_M}$)}\\
&= \frac{\Var{T}}{M} && \text{(cancel one factor of $M$)}\\
\SE{\bar T_M} &= \sqrt{\Var{\bar T_M}} && \text{(standard error is the standard deviation)}\\
&= \frac{\SD{T}}{\sqrt{M}} && \text{(take the square root)}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
